title: A 30% Discount Denial That Turned on an ARR Threshold
scenario_text:
A revenue operations analyst at Merrick Analytics must decide whether a discount request should be approved, given how a similar request was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-02)**
Customer 'Brightwater' | ARR $180K. Requested a 30% discount. Deal Desk DENIED. Note: 'Discounts above 25% require VP Finance approval unless deal ARR is at least $500K, in which case Deal Desk may approve up to 40%. Brightwater is $180K — below the threshold — and no VP approval was obtained. Denied.'

**Current request C (2024-06-11)**
Customer 'Calderwood Group' | ARR $620K | 3-year deal. Requesting a 30% discount to match a competitor. Deal is otherwise clean; no other approvals outstanding.

**Discount Authority Policy (current, unchanged since 2023-11)**
Standard discounts up to 25% are approved by Deal Desk. Discounts above 25% require VP Finance approval, EXCEPT that when a deal's ARR is at least $500K, Deal Desk may approve discounts up to 40% without VP involvement. This threshold-based Deal Desk authority has been in place since November 2023.

**Slack — #revops**
AE: 'We already denied a 30% ask back in February for basically the same discount level. Consistency says we deny Calderwood too.'
Analyst: 'The February deal was tiny — let me look at why it was actually denied before we assume it's precedent.'

The AE wants a quick decision and is treating the February outcome as a blanket rule that 30% is not allowed. No one has yet checked whether Calderwood clears the ARR threshold that changes who can approve.
question: How should the analyst handle Calderwood Group's 30% discount request?
choices: Deny the 30% discount, consistent with the February denial of a similar 30% request.
Approve the 30% discount at Deal Desk, because Calderwood's $620K ARR clears the $500K threshold that lets Deal Desk approve up to 40% — a path the February deal never qualified for.
Escalate to VP Finance for approval, since any discount above 25% requires VP sign-off.
Offer a 25% discount as a compromise to keep the deal within Deal Desk's standard authority.
